The Rc discussed the efficacy of the changed length and strait shape and observed that as there is no change in Chemical Composition, Raw material used, Burn Rate etc. It was observed there is change in shape of preliminary packing box, secondary pack, for which all data has been submitted, hence the case is approved for grant of endorsement of Transfluthrin 0.15% Mosquito coil to Transfluthrin 0.15% Mosquito stick.

Presentation by M/s T. Stanes and company Ltd. regarding follow up action on Agenda Item No. 10.35 of 469th RC meeting. The representatives of the applicant, M/s T. Stanes and Company Ltd., made a detailed presentation before the RC. After hearing the submissions of the applicant, RC observed that Citral and Geraniol are included in the Schedule to the Insecticides Act, 1968. In view of the same, both molecules shall be treated as integral components of the product. The concerned Expert informed that the present application is for grant of registration of Cymbopogan plant extract (containing 1% Geraniol min). It was further elaborated that Cymbopogan plant extract is rich in monoterpenes, specifically citral (α and β), geranial, neral, geraniol, citronellal, and myrcene. It also contains flavonoids, saponins, and phenolic compounds also. It was also observed that Citral has been included in the Schedule to the IA, 1968 vide notification No. S.O. 1854(E) dated 29th April, 2024. As the Citral has been included into the Schedule to the Insecticides Act 1968, hence guidelines of registration and data requirement is applicable. Therefore, the applicant is required to submit complete and updated data for Citral as per guidelines, including the percentage (% w/w) content of Citral in the Chemical Composition (CC) through a revised Form-I, along with Labels/Leaflets (L/Ls) and NJSP. The applicant shall also submit revised Product Specifications specifying the parameters of Citral and Method of Analysis (MOA). All such submissions shall be in accordance with the applicable guidelines and shall be treated as mandatory for further examination by the Registration Committee.

items.decision: The Registration Committee deliberated on the presentation made by the applicant in the 470th RC meeting regarding the proposed formulation. As per the 469th RC minutes, the applicant was invited to make a presentation before the Registration Committee in the 470th meeting to justify the absolute necessity for registration of the proposed formulation. The applicant made the presentation before the Committee. After detailed deliberation, the Registration Committee observed that the applicant has not justified in the presentation that the proposed formulation is an absolute necessity for its registration in view of the recommendations of the Dr. C.D. Mayee Committee. The Committee further observed that the combination belongs to the red toxicity triangle category, whereas the individual formulations of each technical do not fall under the red triangle category. Both Minutes of 470th RC meeting held on 23.03.2026 components are neurotoxicants, and the synergistic effect of the components appears evident. The Committee also noted that safer alternatives are available. The Committee was apprised that if a formulation is more toxic than its technical grade active ingredient, sub-acute toxicity studies are required as per the guidelines and decisions of the Registration Committee (449th RC). Further, the applicant requested to conduct the study again as per OECD 425; however, the Committee was of the view that repeating the study would not add any substantial outcome to the assessment. In view of the above, the Committee concluded that the proposed formulation is not justified for registration and therefore doesn’t qualify for the consideration of grant of registration. Accordingly, the matter is disposed-of.

items.title: Order of Hon’ble appellate authority in appeal no. 12 of 2025 M/s. Drosera International Pvt. Ltd. vs CIB&RC. Fresh revision petition filed by CCFI vs CIB&RC. Representation of ACFI dated 25.02.2026 on the issues of data requirement for 9(3) TI New Source (467th & 468th RC meetings).
items.decision: RC perused the agenda and observed that M/s Drosera International Pvt. Ltd. had filed an appeal against the guidelines for TI New Source issued by the RC in its 467th Meeting at agenda item no. 3.2 wherein it was alleged that the said guidelines inter-alia had adversely affected the appellants rights and legitimate expectations. It was also submitted before the appellate authority that the said guidelines were made applicable retrospectively which is not tenable in the eyes of law. The appellate authority after hearing the appellant and the CIB&RC, had found the appeal to be not admissible, recognizing that the power of the RC flows from section 5 of the Insecticide Act with respect to framing, reviewing and modifying the technical guidelines and therefore are not amenable to the Appellate jurisdiction u/s 10 of the Act. However, the liberty has been granted to the appellant to submit a representation before the RC highlighting its technical concerns/difficulties arising from the said guidelines and the RC may consider and examine the same in accordance with the Law and applicable regulatory framework. RC also perused an email communication dated 13.03.2026 received from Dr. Shilpa Arora Advocate, the counsel of the appellant. RC also perused the representation dated 25.02.2026 submitted by M/s ACFI wherein inter-alia it is stated that the certain scientific requirements pertaining to the shelf-life data, bio efficacy, toxicity may be dispensed with and the requirements as per 449th RC meeting be implemented in a balanced and scientifically justified manner. RC after detailed deliberation observed that the guidelines so formulated in its 467th meeting at agenda item no. 3.2 were subsequently modified in its 468th meeting, wherein the waiver has been granted to the livestock metabolism study and the RC is of the view that the requirements so laid down are scientifically and essentially required for the evaluations of safety and efficacy of the substance proposed to be registered under TI New Source and also these guidelines have been made more transparent and clear so that there may not exist any ambiguity in understanding the data requirements to be followed by the applicant. However certain correction in the guidelines as per scientific requirements are made. The revised guideline is attached as Annexure 3.1.1. The same shall be applicable from the date of publishing the minutes on the website. RC also observed that the requirements so laid down are not as such which are unable to be fulfilled by the applicant. In view of the above deliberation, the RC is of the considered view that the requirements laid down are reasonable and scientifically justified. RC is also of the view that data requirements are Minutes of 470th RC meeting held on 23.03.2026 to be implemented prospectively and shall have no bearing on the existing applications submitted in CROP. Only information is required to be submitted by all the existing/pending applications, extra data required (than existing guidelines) in revised guidelines not to be submitted by the existing applicant. RC also perused the revision petition filled by M/s CCFI on the challenge of the RC decision taken in its 468th meeting at agenda item no 2.2 and agenda item no 1. RC notes that the hearing in the above revision petition has been notified for 06.04.2026 by the Hon’ble Authority. RC directs the concerned technical experts to adequately deal with the matter as appropriate and justified submissions may be made before the Hon’ble Revisional Authority. RC also desired that if any directions are issued by the Hon’ble Authority the same shall be placed before the RC for appropriate compliance.

items.group: Application for registration under section 9(4) FIM/FI/TI.
items.title: Compliance with 469th RC decision-submission of detailed and verified manufacturing address of the source from the overseas country and Geo tagging along with photographs in case of 9(4) TI/ FI applications. The Registration Committee (RC) recalled its decision taken in the 469th RC meeting under Agenda Item No. 3.1, wherein the RC sought the geo-tagging details of the manufacturing location in the overseas country. The RC further observed that the geo-tagging details, duly legalized/apostilled by the competent authority of the respective country, may be considered as a proof along with a location map indicating the place where the manufacturing activities are carried out in that country. However, RC observed that the issues are further required to be looked into in-depth being pertaining to overseas countries vis a vis the issue related to the acceptance/approval of chemical composition etc.
items.decision: The RC directed the Secretary, CIB&RC that any case put-up to RC should be scientifically and legally justified. In view of above RC directs the concerned Experts to bring a detailed agenda clearly mentioning the earlier RC decision on the subject in consultation with the Senior Law Officer on the legal issues that may be involved.

items.decision: RC deliberated the agenda and observed that there is change in the name of the source of import as well as its address/location etc. The RC apprised that there are various categories of applications received in the Sectt. of CIBRC on the issue as under: 1. Endorsement of change of name of source of Import of chemicals due to disinvestment. 2. Change of name of source of import 3. Change of manufacturing site 4. Addition of manufacturing site It was further observed that checklist exists on the above issues. It was also informed that as per checklist there is no requirement of submission of 5 batch sample to CIL in the existing checklist. Even some of the “case to case basis” RC has asked the applicant to do so. items.title: Order dated 02.03.2026 passed by the Division bench of the Madurai Bench of Madras High Court in Writ Appeals no.240 & 241 of 2026 filed by the UOI & others against the Order Minutes of 470th RC meeting held on 23.03.2026 dated 28.11.2025 passed by the Learned Single Judge in WP(MD) no. 32496 & 34177 of 2025.
items.decision: RC perused the agenda and observed that the order dated 28.11.2025 passed by the Learned Single Judge passed in WP No. 32496 and 34177 of 2025 staying the directions dated 15.09.2025 (Paragraph 1) issued by the Union of India (DA&FW) wherein the RC was directed not issue any extension u/s 9(3B) beyond a period of two years as the same is not permitted under the Insecticide Act 1968. The said order dated 28.11.2025 was challenged in an intra-court appeal before the Division Bench of the Hon’ble Madras High Court (Madurai bench) wherein upon hearing the matter on 02.03.2026 the Hon’ble High Court had in the meanwhile directed to maintain a status- quo. RC asked the Senior Law Officer as to what compliance is to be made by the RC in terms of the order dated 02.03.2026. Senior Law Officer had enlightened that since status-quo interim order has been granted on the Writ Appeals filled by the Union of India (DA&FW) and therefore if any extensions has already been granted by the RC, the same may be continued and no further extension are to be considered/granted till the Writ Appeals are finally heard and decided by the Division Bench of Hon’ble High Court. Senior law Officer also apprised that the above Writ Appeals are listed for hearing today i.e. 23.03.2026 and learned ASG shall be appearing on behalf of Union of India. In view of above RC directs the concerned technical expert to maintain a status-quo in the above matters. RC also desired that the Senior law Officer may also apprise the RC of the status of the court proceedings at Hon’ble High Court of Madras (Madurai Bench) so as to ensure appropriate compliance of the directions, if any, issued by the Hon’ble High Court.

items.title: WP No. 29623/2024 M/s GSP Crop Science Pvt Ltd vs UOI & Others at Hon’ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana, Chandigarh. RC Perused the agenda and observed that the matter pertains to the presence of excessive quantity of N-Nitroso Pendimethalin wherein the RC its 459th meeting had kept the CR for the product in abeyance. Challenging the said decision M/s GSP as filled the above Writ Petition before the Hon’ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. The Hon’ble High Court has passed an interim order staying the decision of the RC to the extent to keeping the CR of the product in abeyance. RC also observed that during the pendency of the petition a speaking order was passed by the RC in terms of 461st decision on the subject held on 28.01.2025. RC notes that now the speaking order dated 28.01.2025 has also being challenged before the Hon’ble High Court and an amended Writ Petition has been received from the Hon’ble High Court. RC observed that this issue has also been dealt by the RC in 467th meeting at agenda item no 3.3 wherein inter-alia the RC has fixed the limits of N-Nitroso Pendimethalin. RC also observed that an appropriate method of analysis already exists for the subject substance which was used by the CIL while analysing the sample. The same is placed at Annexure-10.12.1. RC directs the Secretariat of CIB&RC to appropriately deal with the matter and the scientific justification for the impugned speaking order may be apprised to the Hon’ble High Court as the matter pertains to the issues related to Public Health. The method of analysis adopted for the substance should also be put in public domain.

items.title: Submission of fake document/test report by M/s Sunshine fine Chemsol (I) Pvt Ltd. Follow up of agenda item no 10.6 of 468th RC decision held on 12.01.2026.
items.decision: RC perused the agenda and observed that the applicant has submitted a response to the show cause notice issued to the applicant on the issue of submitting fake /forged report as recorded by the RC in its decision taken in its 468th meeting at agenda item no 10.6. RC also perused the response dated 23.01.2026 submitted by the applicant wherein it is inter-alia submitted about the ignorance of the submission of the captioned forged report. RC observed that the issue pertains to the forgery of documents and obtaining a CR which is a valuable security on the basis of fake documents/report which is an extremely serious issue and tanta-mounts to suppression of truth and expression of falsehood which is prima-facie seen and is writ large in the present matter. RC is also of the view that mere ignorance can’t be accepted on its face value unless supported by some clinching evidence which is not found to be enclosed by the applicant with their response. RC also notes that the applicant vide communication dated 23.02.2026 had requested to grant them an opportunity to present their matter before taking any decision. RC is also of the view that secretariat of CIB&RC to also seek factual status in terms of the response submitted from the then concerned toxicology expert who had dealt with the matter. RC is of the further view that in the interest of justice and transparency the applicant may be called a presentation in the next RC meeting.

items.title: Follow up action of minutes of the Senior Officers meeting held on 09.03.2026 under the chairmanship of Secretary, DA&FW. Minutes of 470th RC meeting held on 23.03.2026 For bio-pesticide, revised guidelines to be finalized by first week of April, 2026. The time period and procedure for registration of pesticides licensing process should be rationalized & reformed for ease of doing business. Registration Committee (RC) has already simplified the guidelines for bio-pesticides. Provisional registration is granted under Section 9(3B) of the Insecticides Act, 1968 with permission for commercialization for two years, extendable for generating required data for regular registration under Section 9(3). Further, where a bio- pesticide strain is already registered in the country, no fresh data is required from new applicants, except confirmation of molecular identity from ICAR-NBAIM, Maunath Bhanjan (UP), and quality testing from the Central Insecticide Laboratory (CIL). The matter was deliberated during the 470th RC Meeting held on 23.03.2026. RC has observed that a significant bottleneck exists at the ICAR- NBAIM, Mau, specifically concerning the mandatory 1600s RNA molecular identification and DNA sequencing required for biopesticides (microbial). To address this and rationalize the registration procedure, the RC has proposed exploring additional institutes, such as ICAR-NBAIR in Bengaluru, which possess the necessary facilities for such identifications. By enabling the submission of samples to two institutes instead of one, the RC aims to significantly reduce the current pendency and streamline the registration process. A communication may be sent to the ICAR- NBAIR, Bengaluru to know their capabilities in the matter. Further, Sectt. Of CIB&RC has already issued strict instructions to all technical experts to complete the scrutiny of all files that have been pending for more than 18 months. These files are currently being scrutinized at an accelerated pace by all experts to ensure that the backlog is cleared within the stipulated time period.

items.title: Consideration of an application of M/s BASF India Ltd for the registration of Alphacypermethrin 30g/l+ Flufenoxuron 30 g/l SC formulation for Import for household u/s 9(3). RC was apprised that the product is intended to be registered for effective control of Bed Bugs, Houseflies, and Cockroaches across a wide range of indoor environments. Its recommended areas of application include office buildings, commercial kitchens, hospitals, schools, hotels, and various other household and public spaces where insect infestations may pose hygiene, safety, or comfort concerns. Applicant has not submitted the health monitoring study which is the requirement for registration of pesticides for household purpose. Justification for exemption submitted by the applicant is not considered scientifically valid. Moreover, conduct of health monitoring study is a long-drawn process which involves the protocol submission by the applicant, approval by registration committee and conduct of the study adhering to the protocol/guidelines. In view of the above, the application stands closed for now and applicant may reapply with the health monitoring study. The data/scrutiny comments of the closed/revived file will be taken into account with the subsequent file. Meeting ended with vote of thanks to the chair. *****
